servicePage.box_title: The system shut down without closing
servicePage.box_in_job: The machine was working when it cut out: check the piece before going on.
servicePage.box_v_calm_t: Most likely: the power was cut at once
servicePage.box_v_calm_d: Up to the last reading everything was normal (CPU max {cpu} %, memory {ram} %, {temp} °C): no overload and no heat. So the most likely cause is that power stopped reaching the Pi (cable, plug, supply or meter) and not that the Pi failed. This is an estimate.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_t: Most likely: the service was already stuck before the cut
servicePage.box_v_stuck_d: The last reading showed something stuck: {thing}. A task that does not move for minutes leaves the Pi slow or unresponsive, and the cut came afterwards. It does not look like heat or memory (CPU max {cpu} %, memory {ram} %, {temp} °C).
servicePage.box_v_heat_d: It reached {temp} °C in the last {min} min. Check the ventilation and the heat sink of the Pi.
servicePage.box_v_load_t: The Pi was at its CPU limit
servicePage.box_v_load_d: The CPU was near {cpu} % in the last readings. A hang from load is possible; see which processes were heavy in the Processes section.
servicePage.box_v_memory_d: Memory reached {ram} %. A hang from lack of memory is possible.
servicePage.box_v_mixed_d: CPU up to {cpu} %, memory up to {ram} %, {temp} °C at most. Look at the charts and the lines below.
servicePage.box_v_without_data_d: The cut came very soon after power-on, or the black box did not manage to save readings.
servicePage.box_todo: So it does not happen again
servicePage.air_rule: Turns on with M3/M4 and turns off a few seconds after M5.
servicePage.mov_card_sub: Who may move the machine (jog, Workbench, Vision...) while a cut is running.
servicePage.mov_opt_nobody_d: During a live cut or while the bridge sends orders, the jog, the Workbench and Vision move nothing.
servicePage.mov_opt_me_d: Only a file job blocks, as in DWC. You can move by hand during a live cut. Machine settings stay protected.
servicePage.mov_release_d: without bridge orders: the jog, the Workbench and Vision can move again (if the live job is still open, they ask to confirm first). It is the first step; the second is "Finish after" in Live job, which closes the job. Less than 8 s is risky: a slow program can leave the machine still for a few seconds between passes.
servicePage.live_end_intro: When it counts as finished: at once when the program sends the end signal; if it does not, by idle time.
servicePage.live_end_note: of rest and no activity. It is the second step, after "Consider it free after" (Machine movement): it closes the live job record, counts hours and kWh up to the last activity and releases the block, without asking to confirm. It does not stop the machine. Keep it equal to or longer than the other time.
servicePage.box_charts_note: The last minutes before shutting down (saved data, not live). The live charts are in System health.
servicePage.box_now_d: This already happened. The Pi started again by itself, so you do not need to do anything to get back to normal. If the Duet board also lost power, home the machine before moving or cutting.
servicePage.box_now_hide: This notice stays until you press Hide. If it happens again, a new one appears.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s1: Check that the power cable of the Pi and the plug are firm and do not move when touched.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s2: Open Consumption and look at the chart for that hour: if the power drops to 0 at once, the power was cut; if it keeps reading, the Pi restarted by itself.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s3: Check in the meter app whether a schedule or timer turns that plug off.
servicePage.box_v_calm_s4: If it happens again, try another 5 V supply and cable, and do not share them with motors or the heated bed.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s1: Look in Pi service for the process that was slow or not beating and restart it if it stays that way.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s2: Check the bridge and the communication with the Duet: a long lock usually comes from an order that never finishes.
servicePage.box_v_stuck_s3: If it happens again, download this report and compare it with the service log at that hour.
servicePage.box_v_heat_s1: Clean the dust and check that the fan and the heat sink of the Pi are in place.
servicePage.box_v_heat_s2: Leave free space around the case and do not cover it.
servicePage.box_v_heat_s3: Look at the temperature in System health: at rest it should stay below 60 °C.
servicePage.box_v_load_s1: Open Processes and see which one used the most CPU.
servicePage.box_v_load_s2: If it was an open page or a very large preview, close it and try again calmly.
servicePage.box_v_load_s3: If it happens again, download these lines and keep them.
servicePage.box_v_memory_s1: Open Processes and see which one used the most memory.
servicePage.box_v_memory_s2: Restart the heaviest service from Processes.
servicePage.box_v_memory_s3: If it happens again, download these lines and keep them.
servicePage.box_v_mixed_s1: Look at the charts and the lines below.
servicePage.box_v_mixed_s2: Check the power cable and look at the Consumption chart for that hour.
servicePage.box_v_mixed_s3: Download the lines and keep them in case it happens again.
servicePage.box_v_without_data_s1: Leave the system on for a few minutes and look again.
servicePage.box_v_without_data_s2: If it shuts down again right after power-on, check the supply and the cable.

page.interceptorDesc: Answers the API of the pages and programs, runs the processes below and publishes the state for the pages.
page.liveJobDesc: A program that sends the job line by line, without a file on the Duet, over the network or the USB of the board. It is marked with BRIDGE JOB START <name> in its start G-code and BRIDGE JOB END at the end (G-code bridge), or with the API operations job.start / job.end; it is kept in Activity and blocks the jog while it runs.
page.apiHelp: Pages, macros and external programs call these operations with POST /machine/WorkshopService/api (JSON with op and args). Macros use M98 P"0:/sys/workshop/macros/service-call.g" S"<operation>" (only the ones marked for macros).
page.service_lead: What runs under every page: background processes, the link to the board, API and keys.

keys.title: Access keys (external services)
keys.intro: A key lets an external program or service (an app, a phone, another computer) use the API with the permissions you choose, without giving it the DWC password. Each service has its own and it can be switched off or deleted without affecting the others.
keys.how_to_use: The service sends the key in the X-Workshop-Key header of every request to POST /machine/WorkshopService/api. A key can never use the administration operations (keys, password, restoring configurations).

keys.expired_hint: Expired: it does not work even if it is on. Edit it to give it more days.
keys.classes_help: Read = query. Change = write settings, lights, notices. Move = move the machine. Stop = stops. Power = power off and restart.

procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_what: The RS485 plugin process: it talks to servos and other Modbus devices over the serial ports of the Pi.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_how: It opens each configured bus, polls the devices in turns and publishes their state in the machine model; the RS485 page reads it from there. It keeps backups and a history of what it sees.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_depends: The RS485 plugin enabled in Settings > Plugins, free serial ports, and devices connected and powered.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopRS485_why: Because the RS485 plugin is enabled. If you stop it in Settings > Plugins this process stops with it.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_what: The vision engine (OpenCV): it analyses camera images to measure parts, find marks and detect smoke.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_how: It asks the camera relay for pictures only when someone needs them and drops the stream after 30 s without requests; it uses the saved calibration to turn pixels into millimetres.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_depends: The Vision plugin enabled, the camera relay (Camera or Workbench plugin) and the camera calibration.
procDocs.ext_WorkshopVision_why: Because the Vision plugin is enabled; at rest it uses almost nothing (about 0.1 % CPU).
procDocs.ext_base_what: The SQLite database of the service: activity history, consumption, presets and received commands.
procDocs.ext_base_how: A single file on the Pi; the other processes write there and the pages query it through the API. It repairs itself if it finds badly saved dates.
procDocs.ext_base_depends: The disk of the Pi and the Workshop service; it needs no plugin.
procDocs.ext_base_why: Because the service always needs it to keep the history.
procDocs.ext_bridge_what: The program on the Pi that lets other programs (for example the laser software) send G-code to the Duet over the network, through the Telnet port.
procDocs.ext_bridge_how: It listens on the configured port, receives the G-code lines of each connected program and passes them to the Duet; it tells the page when a live job starts and ends.
procDocs.ext_bridge_depends: On the workshop-gcode-bridge service being installed and active on the Pi (installed with install.sh), on the network and on the port being free.
procDocs.ext_bridge_why: Because it is installed and enabled on the Pi. It is only needed to send live jobs from an outside program; if you do not use it, it can be stopped.
procDocs.interceptor_what: Watches the M3, M4 and M5 G-codes that go through the board as they happen.
procDocs.interceptor_why: Turns the air assist on only when the laser turns on and off a few seconds after M5, so nobody has to remember it.
procDocs.interceptor_fails: The air no longer turns on and off by itself; the laser keeps working the same. It restarts by itself.
procDocs.interceptor_uses: The DSF connection (code interception) and the air relay (output 7).
procDocs.interceptor_where: Automations > Automatic air with the laser.
procDocs.status_light_what: Paints the status zone of the LED strip and works out the indicator the screens show.
procDocs.status_light_why: Shows at a glance what the machine is doing (idle, job, pause, risk) with a colour and an effect, on the strip and in the bar.
procDocs.status_light_fails: The status LEDs keep the last colour or the board fallback takes over; the screens stop showing the indicator.
procDocs.status_light_uses: The board object model, the M150 commands and the rules of the Lights and status page.
procDocs.status_light_where: Lights and status page. It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.consumption_what: Reads the Tuya energy meter (W, V, A and accumulated kWh).
procDocs.consumption_why: Stores the consumption history so the cost per day, month or job can be worked out.
procDocs.consumption_fails: No new readings are saved; the chart shows a gap. What was already saved is kept.
procDocs.consumption_uses: The Tuya meter over the local network and the database.
procDocs.consumption_where: Power page (rate and meter). It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.jobs_what: Detects when a job starts and ends, the mode changes or the work zone changes.
procDocs.jobs_why: Feeds the Activity history, the phone alerts and the hours and energy per job.
procDocs.jobs_fails: Job starts and ends are not recorded; Activity and the alerts stop hearing about them.
procDocs.jobs_uses: The machine state (single subscription) and the database.
procDocs.motors_what: Works out the pulse frequency, RPM, speed and driver state of each motor.
procDocs.motors_why: Shows how close to its limit each motor works and whether a driver reports a problem.
procDocs.motors_fails: The Motors page stops updating. Movement is not affected.
procDocs.motors_uses: The object model, M122 and a read-only read of the GSTAT register.
procDocs.motors_where: Motors page. It rests when that plugin is stopped.
procDocs.jog_what: Moves the machine while a jog control is held.
procDocs.jog_why: Turns the knob, the arrows and the keyboard into short chained moves with the laser off.
procDocs.jog_fails: Jog stops moving; the rest of the machine is unaffected. If the screen heartbeat stops arriving, the movement cuts itself.
procDocs.jog_uses: Its own connection to the board and the motion owner.
procDocs.events_what: Watches the board messages: emergencies, pauses, errors and warnings.
procDocs.events_why: Stores them in Activity and sends them to the phone when needed.
procDocs.events_fails: Emergency, pause and error alerts are lost while it is stopped.
procDocs.events_uses: The object model messages (single subscription) and the notifier.
procDocs.trace_what: Records the path of the running job.
procDocs.trace_why: Lets Zones > Job draw the path. It only records while someone is watching; otherwise it sleeps.
procDocs.trace_fails: The job path is not drawn. The job itself is not affected.
procDocs.trace_uses: The object model (position) and files on the SD.
procDocs.health_what: Measures the Pi temperature, WiFi, services and power supply.
procDocs.health_why: Warns before something fails: high temperature, WiFi down, a stopped service or an unexpected reboot.
procDocs.health_fails: The Health page and its alerts stop updating.
procDocs.health_uses: System commands (vcgencmd, nmcli, systemctl) and the object model.
procDocs.camera_what: Shares the camera video with all screens and records the timelapses.
procDocs.camera_why: Prevents every screen from opening its own connection to the weak camera.
procDocs.camera_fails: The shared video and new timelapses are lost.
procDocs.camera_uses: The ESP32-CAM camera, ffmpeg and the SD.
procDocs.camera_where: Camera page. The relay is shared with Vision and Workbench.
procDocs.timer_what: Counts down the timed shutdown of the bar.
procDocs.timer_why: Turns everything off at the chosen time, without cutting a running job.
procDocs.timer_fails: The scheduled shutdown does not run.
procDocs.timer_uses: The system clock and the power cut.
procDocs.risk_what: Detects when something leaves the machine without a protection: calibrations and released motors.
procDocs.risk_why: Warns on screens and LEDs for as long as the risk lasts and clears itself when it ends.
procDocs.risk_fails: The risk is not announced. The board protections are unchanged.
procDocs.risk_uses: The object model and the flags set by the calibration macros.
procDocs.risk_where: No settings: it turns on when calibrating or releasing motors.
procDocs.config_guard_what: Watches the board start-up after a new configuration is saved.
procDocs.config_guard_why: Goes back to the previous configuration if the start-up fails or nobody confirms.
procDocs.config_guard_fails: A bad configuration would not be reverted by itself.
procDocs.config_guard_uses: The config.g backup and the board state.
procDocs.motion_what: Decides whether the machine may move or change its geometry, and why not.
procDocs.motion_why: Prevents two things from moving at once (jog, macros, job) and explains the block.
procDocs.motion_fails: The pages do not know whether a move is in progress and may allow too much or too little.
procDocs.motion_uses: The object model, the screen heartbeats and the bridge.
procDocs.motion_where: No settings: used by Jog, Zones and the macros.
procDocs.subscription_what: Keeps the single DSF subscription with the machine state.
procDocs.subscription_why: It is the source every other process reads from, so nobody asks the board for the state on its own.
procDocs.subscription_fails: The processes keep old data until it reconnects, which it does by itself.
procDocs.subscription_where: See patches/s and KB/s under 'Load this service puts on the Duet'.
procDocs.box_black_what: Writes a line every few seconds with load, CPU, RAM, temperature and state to the SD.
procDocs.box_black_why: If the Pi hangs or is switched off by force, there is a record of the last moments.
procDocs.box_black_fails: No trail is kept; after a hang the cause will not be known.
procDocs.box_black_uses: Files on the SD (two of 512 KB, rotating).
procDocs.auto_air_what: Turns the air assist on with M3 or M4 and off a few seconds after M5.
procDocs.auto_air_when: When the laser turns on in a cut (M3/M4).
procDocs.auto_air_note: With the switch off, the air is only handled by hand or by the program. The delay avoids turning the air off between two consecutive strokes.
procDocs.auto_lights_what: The status LED strip paints itself according to the mode and what the machine is doing.
procDocs.auto_lights_note: The lights are controlled in the Lights and status page; here you only see the result. With the manual lighting on, those LEDs are used by the work light.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_what: When the job ends it turns everything off and cuts the machine power.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_when: When the running job ends, or the next one if there is none.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_note: It is only armed and disarmed here or in the side bar; it never cuts a running job. It cuts the power through the Tuya meter: make sure nothing must stay on.
procDocs.auto_poweroff_note_no_bar: It is only armed and disarmed here; it never cuts a running job. It cuts the power through the Tuya meter: make sure nothing must stay on.
procDocs.auto_job_what: Marks the live job sent by an external program through the G-code bridge.
procDocs.auto_job_when: It starts with the material macro (livemark.g) or the line M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB START name". It ends with M118 P0 S"BRIDGE JOB END", on stop or cancel, if the machine halts, or after the chosen rest time. Also with the job.start and job.end operations of the API.
procDocs.auto_job_note: The idle timeout closes a job that was left open and adds its hours and kWh. While there is one, jog and zones are locked so nothing moves the machine in the middle of the cut.
procDocs.ui_cadence_help: Average time between heartbeats compared with what is expected. Up to 100 % is normal; above it the process is falling behind.
procDocs.ui_summary_unavailable: Not available: the service is not connected
procDocs.guard_what: Checks that the safety processes keep beating: status lights, camera relay, board events, motion, risk, health, Vision and RS485.
procDocs.guard_why: If one dies the protection disappears unnoticed and the light strip could stay green with the machine in fault.
procDocs.guard_fails: Nobody watches the watchers: the status lights show the warning if this process stops.
procDocs.guard_uses: This service's heartbeats, the answer of Vision and the RS485 data.
procDocs.guard_where: API operations guard.status and guard.set (the safe action is to warn or to pause the job).

users.disabled_help: The people are still saved, but nobody has to identify: anybody with access to DWC is an administrator and the camera and Vision are open on the network. Switch them on again whenever you want.
users.off_help: Turns the roles and PINs off without deleting anybody. It needs your PIN. While they are off everybody is an administrator and the camera is open on the network.
users.off_dialog_help: Type your administrator PIN to confirm. Every session will end.
users.title: People
users.help: Each person logs in with a name and a PIN. The role decides what they can do: Visitor looks at the state, Operator moves and cuts in the allowed modes, Technician calibrates and changes settings, Administrator manages people, keys and shutdown. The service enforces it, not just the screen.
users.no_users_notice: No users: anyone with access to DWC is an administrator.
users.disabled_notice: Users switched off: anyone with access to DWC is an administrator.
users.wizard_help: Create the first person, who will be an administrator. From then on everybody has to identify with a name and a PIN. Write the PIN down: if it is forgotten, the users file has to be deleted on the Raspberry to start over.
users.pins_differ: The two PINs are not the same.
users.not_identified: You have not identified yourself in this browser.
users.admin_only: Only an administrator sees this section.
users.name: Name
users.reset_help: It ends their open sessions. Tell them the new PIN in person.
users.modes_help: An operator only moves and runs jobs in the checked modes (laser only by default). Changing the mode is for the technician.
users.never_expires_help: On: a session ends only when the person logs out or the service restarts; the two limits below are ignored.
users.camera_for_viewers_help: Off: a visitor sees the state of the machine but not the camera.
users.anonymous_viewer: Without logging in, only look at the state
users.anonymous_viewer_help: For the touch screen of the workshop: whoever does not log in can see the state as a visitor, never move or change anything.

audit.title: Audit
audit.help: Who did what, from which device: changes, refused attempts and logins. Read only; nobody can delete it from here, it only cleans itself by age.
